note: Every entry is a KNOWN divergence between the Web fallback layer and desktop Obsidian 1.13.7. The gate fails when a divergence is not listed here, when a listed divergence no longer matches the recorded values, or when a listed token starts matching (stale entry). Classes: notation (same intent, different CSS), value-drift (stale copy of a desktop value), structural (needs a Web feature, not a value edit), web-invention (no desktop counterpart), web-only (not a desktop token).

entries.reason: Desktop declares the `-theme` font slots as the `'??'` placeholder and composes the real stack through `--font-interface: override, theme, var(--default-font, '??'), var(--font-default)`. The Web fallback writes its stack directly into the theme slot. Same effective families, different composition — adopted deliberately so a community theme can still override the slot.
Same placeholder composition as `--font-interface-theme`; desktop composes through `--font-monospace`.
Same placeholder composition as `--font-interface-theme`; desktop composes through `--font-text`.

Not an Obsidian core token. Desktop core reads `--file-line-width`; `--line-width` is a community-theme convention (Things and Minimal both declare `--line-width: 40rem`). The Web app consumes only the theme convention, so the core knob — and any theme that sets it — has no effect on Web reading width.
